architecture.notes: O1 largely resolved: PARTICIPANTS is gone and agent_policy() is the single participation source, with a policy fingerprint and a principal/capability/authorization split. The remaining gap is that capability_verified and principal are self-asserted fields inside an unkeyed self-hash binding (N4). O2 partially resolved: legacy rows are kept unmutated and bound by a separate v2 object. No existing QA producer can satisfy the QA coverage rule, and context hashing differs from council_runtime.binding (N1, N5). O3 partially resolved: explicit states and history exist. advance_objection is not consumed by evaluate, so there are two closure mechanisms (N2). The history contract has gaps: it is caller-supplied, and the cross-candidate path has no migration, so it is either bypassable or a dead end (N3). These are architectural contract gaps, not a bypass of production, since the gate stays inactive and all activation flags are false.

objections.claim: The existing controller context (council_runtime.binding) and the new gate both define context.participation_sha256, but they hash the same policy with different serializations, so the values differ for the same policy. A context produced by the real binding() would always yield participation_policy_changed. binding() also does not emit permissions_sha256, which the gate requires. The tests build both sides with code_review._hash, so the mismatch is invisible. This is the same failure mode as the original O2: fixtures hide a real producer shape.
objections.impact: The optional gate cannot consume a real controller context, and a field with one name has two meanings. The first integration attempt will return needs_evidence with a misleading reason.
objections.recommendation: Use one shared canonical-hash helper for participation_sha256, or give the new field a distinct name. Document the full context shape the gate requires. Add a test that feeds the output of council_runtime.binding() (extended with permissions) into the gate.
objections.resolution_condition: A test uses real binding() output, or the two hashes are provably the same function, and the required context fields are documented in one place.

evidence_refs: evaluate computes closed from `answers` (a bare list) plus any bound resolution receipt

objections.claim: There are two independent closure paths. The advance_objection state machine (author_answered, review_pending, refuted/resolved) is not consumed by the gate. evaluate closes a finding with an unauthenticated `answers` entry plus a resolution receipt, and ignores the record, its event order and resolution_state. A resolution binding can close a finding without any author_answered, new_evidence or review_pending transition ever having been recorded. The answer is not bound to the candidate or to the author.
objections.impact: The state machine documented as the O3 resolution contract is not what enforces closure. Behaviour validated by the state-machine tests is not the behaviour that gates approval.
objections.recommendation: Make evaluate take objection records (or their derived state) as input and close only when the record is terminal with a valid confirmation. Alternatively, remove advance_objection and document the receipt-only closure. Bind answers to the candidate hash.
objections.resolution_condition: One closure mechanism is enforced by evaluate, with a test showing a resolution receipt without a prior author answer record does not close.

evidence_refs: review_history defaults to () and is caller-supplied; no completeness or chain check
prior_candidate_review_requires_migration is emitted but no function consumes or clears it
same-candidate history is merged only after the stale_review/unverified_reviewer `continue` paths
test_O3_different_candidate_does_not_erase_adverse_history asserts only the missing marker
objections.claim: The adverse-history protection depends on the caller passing complete history. Omitting it, which is the default, erases the prior changes_requested. The cross-candidate path has no clearing contract, so with complete history a corrected candidate can never leave needs_evidence. Same-candidate history of a reviewer is merged only after earlier `continue` branches. A reviewer whose envelope is stale, unverified or absent leaves a prior BLOCKER or HIGH out of blockers and changes, and the state degrades to needs_evidence.
objections.impact: The gate is either bypassable by omitting history or a dead end for any corrected diff after an adverse review. A BLOCKER can be reported as only needs_evidence.
objections.recommendation: Define a controller-store loader that returns the complete history for the objection lineage, and fail closed if it is not provided. Specify the migration receipt that lets a new candidate carry forward a resolved prior finding. Evaluate history for every expected reviewer before the envelope `continue` branches.
objections.resolution_condition: A test shows that omitted history is rejected (or comes from a store handle), that a defined migration clears a prior-candidate finding, and that a prior BLOCKER yields blocked even when the current envelope is unverified.

evidence_refs: bind_receipt accepts any principal dict and stores a copy

objections.claim: bind_receipt is a public function that mints a binding for any principal dict the caller supplies. The binding hash is unkeyed and the legacy row hash is recomputable, so whoever can call it can mint a row and a binding that make an arbitrary reviewer, capability and supersession list appear verified. The docstrings state that the controller supplies these, but nothing in evaluate or checked_bindings distinguishes store-loaded bindings from caller-built ones. The trust boundary is therefore the same as before the change, while the result name suggests stronger proof. The approval-relevant supersedes list lives inside the identity object.
objections.impact: The O1 identity and capability separation is a consistency check, not verification. Approved states depend on a boundary the code does not enforce or label.
objections.recommendation: State the boundary in the result, for example a trust_basis field naming the unauthenticated inputs. Better, accept only a controller-store handle, or add a keyed MAC held by the controller. Move supersedes_review_ids out of principal into a separate binding field.
objections.resolution_condition: The result or API makes the trust basis explicit, and supersession lineage is not part of the identity object.

summary: Changes requested. I did not run the tests; the 60-test result is supplied and not independently verified. Status of the earlier objections. O1 is largely resolved: PARTICIPANTS is gone, agent_policy() is the single registry, and a policy change invalidates the context. Two non-author reviewers remain required, and Antigravity is not enabled. The identity, capability and authorization checks are self-asserted in an unkeyed binding (N4). O2 is partially resolved: legacy rows are preserved and bound separately. No real QA producer can satisfy the coverage rule (N5), and participation_sha256 is computed differently from council_runtime.binding, which the fixtures hide (N1). O3 is partially resolved: explicit states and history exist. The state machine is not what closes findings in evaluate (N2). History is caller-supplied, and the cross-candidate path has no clearing contract, so the gate is either bypassable or a dead end. A prior BLOCKER can also degrade to needs_evidence (N3). O6 is unchanged (N7). No finding shows a production or activation bypass: the gate is not integrated, the activation flags stay false, and council.py is additive. The remaining issues are contract gaps in the optional gate. Favourable review here is not an integration authorization.
